name: Ignition
label: Dischord
lede: Alec MacKaye and Chris Bald took what was left of Faith, added a Gray Matter drummer and a bassist who sometimes reached for a saxophone, and spent three years playing sets that could end in wreckage. The twenty-six songs they left behind fit on one CD.

eras.title: Faith, rewired
eras.text: By 1986 the first wave of D.C. hardcore had burned out, and the next one was feeling its way toward something more melodic and more exposed. Two veterans of Faith tried again, one of them on a new instrument.

years.h: Alec MacKaye and Chris Bald of Faith start Ignition
years.p: Bald switches from bass to guitar. [[Dante Ferrando|98b1e2a2-3868-47f0-b905-35637b5a902f]], who has drummed for [[Iron Cross|13afe528-54f1-4955-bbec-a4bafb590edb]] and [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]], takes the kit, and [[Chris Thomson|e79601f0-2aa6-415c-886e-570aea8acea1]], listed by Dischord as ex-[[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], plays bass with the odd blast of saxophone.
years.xp:
Both front-line members had history. MacKaye, [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]'s younger brother, is the kid with the X-marked hands on the cover of the Teen Idles' Minor Disturbance, and had sung in the Untouchables and Faith. Bald had followed most of Faith into [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], which had just come apart.

AllMusic dates the start to summer 1986; Dischord just says 1986.

eras.title: Combustible from the first night
eras.text: Ignition was a live band first. The University of Maryland's D.C. punk archive remembers "chaotic, earnest, combustible performances," and the band put out its own single before Dischord gave it a number.

yt: Live at Mississippi Nights, St. Louis, June 3, 1987
years.h: Ignition plays its first show at d.c. space
years.p: Dischord dates the debut to spring 1987, at the downtown D.C. arts space and club. The clip is a later set from the same year, in St. Louis.
years.xp: The footage is a 33-minute multicamera set at Mississippi Nights in St. Louis on June 3, 1987, shot for the KDHX cable TV channel.

years.h: Ignition puts out its own single, Anger Means, as Dischord 26½
years.p: Backed with Proven Hollow and produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] engineering. Discogs lists it as a joint IG/Dischord release on blue and gold vinyl.
years.xp:
It was one of two early singles. AllMusic names the pair as Sinker and Anger Means and dates them to early 1988; Discogs lists the Anger Means pressings as 1987.

A full set recorded in Odense, Denmark, on October 24, 1987, includes both songs from the single.

years.cap: Flyer for the Wilson Center benefit, September 3, 1987: Fugazi, Marginal Man, Ignition, Fire Party
years.h: Ignition is on the bill the night [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] debuts
years.p: A benefit at the Wilson Center for Dischord's State of the Union comp: [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]], Ignition, Fire Party and a brand-new trio playing its first show. About 300 people paid $5.

years.h: "So Moved" and "Sinker" live in St. Louis, June 3, 1987
yt: "So Moved" and "Sinker" live in St. Louis, June 3, 1987

eras.title: Two records, a European trip, then the end
eras.text: Ignition toured hard, including a long European run that made it one of the first Dischord bands to play overseas. Two records later, it was done.

years.p: Cut at Inner Ear in February and May 1988 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing. Dischord dates the release to September, and a cassette went out the same year.

years.h: Dischord 032 collects the benefit's bands, Ignition among them
years.p: Two years after the Wilson Center night, State of the Union is out. Ignition contributes Anger Means, next to [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]], [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]] and [[Fidelity Jones|c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717]].

years.h: Dischord 039 runs six songs and is called The Orafying Mysticle of... Ignition
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear in May 1989, this time with [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] producing. Dischord calls it the band's second full-length.
years.xp: AllMusic has it as an EP that appeared in early 1990 and spelled the end of the group. Dischord dates it to 1989.

years.p: The University of Maryland's D.C. punk archive dates the end to 1989, after two records and a handful of singles.
years.xp: The shows stayed unpredictable to the end. Dischord recalls one that finished before the band had completed a single song, after Bald smashed his guitar and amp in frustration: "possibly the shortest set ever played by a DC band."

eras.title: Afterlives, and one CD
eras.text: The four scattered into some of the most durable projects in the city, including the Black Cat nightclub. Dischord kept the records alive by folding them onto a single CD, then remastering it.

years.h: Thomson goes to Circus Lupus, Alec MacKaye to the Warmers
years.p: Thomson fronts [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]], then forms [[The Monorchid|69dbd702-9073-49dd-b73a-67c33f030a4f]] and [[Skull Kontrol|0e327a14-3b74-4635-a9fa-b9060b3acd13]]. Alec MacKaye sings and plays guitar in [[The Warmers|af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f]] with [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]] through the mid-'90s.

years.big: "I like spaces where you can see the band, and you're in the same room with them."
yt: Alec MacKaye sings Anger Means with Give at the Black Cat
years.h: Dante Ferrando opens the Black Cat on 14th Street
years.p: Ferrando, who has played in Ignition, Iron Cross and Gray Matter, told Pollstar that's how he grew up. The Black Cat was still his club more than three decades on.
years.xp:
The club opened in September 1993 at 1831 14th St. NW, in a space that had been a restaurant-club called the Calabash. Ferrando raised the money from family and fellow musicians, former Scream drummer Dave Grohl among them, and told the City Paper none of them were "trying to come up with a sensible investment."

It ran on a shoestring: "We didn't have the money to do real remodeling." The first show was the Fall with Slant 6 on September 16, 1993. The liquor license, he said, was "torturous" and didn't arrive until January 1994.

years.h: Complete Services puts 26 tracks on one disc
years.p: Dischord 088 gathers every Ignition record, all of them originally vinyl or cassette only. Dischord says it adds an unreleased cover of the Vibrators' Keep It Clean.

years.h: Ignition gets a slot on 20 Years of Dischord
years.p: The label's three-disc birthday box includes a track from Ignition.
[[TJ Lipple|ed4cd729-b4d2-4016-a0b6-c362b68d2afb]] masters the CD anew, and Dischord reissues it in June in limited quantities.
He's interviewed in the D.C. punk documentary. His day job, per Wikipedia: chief preparator at the Phillips Collection.

sources.title: Pollstar: Clubland, Dante Ferrando and the Black Cat
